A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVMAE/MVMAE-V2T study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original disease-classification, label-efficiency, calibration and view-count experiments across chest-radiography datasets, including supplementary results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results, revises the main quantitative tables and adds runtime measurements and a preliminary alignment-objective comparison in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The architecture, reconstruction and alignment objectives, modality embeddings, text decoder and inference procedure remain unchanged. Equation 6 introduces a text-loss coefficient gamma, but Appendix B fixes it at 1, preserving v1's objective. The specified annealing parameters add implementation detail.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, PadChest and Chest X-ray for pretraining, with the same three downstream classification datasets and retained label-scarcity and view-count scenarios. The new view-distribution table describes existing coverage.

E2.justification: BiomedCLIP is removed from the Top-5 comparison in Table 2, although retained in other comparisons. Appendix B newly reports a preliminary comparison against InfoNCE alignment. The principal benchmark methods otherwise remain the same.

E3.justification: Section 3 replaces the stated 256×256 resizing, center-cropping and intensity-normalization pipeline with a description specifying only 224×224 resizing; this revises the reported preprocessing without establishing reruns. The new timing comparison specifies matched infrastructure, 500 epochs and 16 nodes. Existing splits and downstream evaluation designs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B investigates alignment overhead through a controlled runtime comparison and reports qualitatively similar preliminary outcomes for MSE and InfoNCE alignment. Existing label-efficiency and view-count analyses are retained. The alignment comparison provides no quantitative breakdown.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 replace point-only reporting with explicitly identified means and standard deviations across three seeds; Table 3 also adds uncertainty quantities. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting for the principal results. v1 already reported three-seed averages for the view-count experiment, so an increase in run counts is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 substantially revise estimates and rankings. Table 1 replaces BiomedCLIP's Combined AUROC of 78.95 with 83.97 ± 0.78. Table 3 changes MVMAE's Combined Brier score from 0.0759 to 0.0835 ± 0.0007, reversing its ranking against Supervised, whose Combined score remains 0.0815. Appendix B adds runtimes of 19,555 seconds for Independent and 19,601 for MVMAE; Table 4 adds view counts. Existing per-label and view-count result tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss formulations remain substantively equivalent, with no new assumptions, derivations or proofs. The explicit gamma in Equation 6 is fixed at 1 in Appendix B and therefore reproduces the earlier objective.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly presents MVMAE as adapting established reconstruction and alignment paradigms. The conclusion qualifies MVMAE-V2T's low-label performance benefit as occurring after full finetuning. The central contributions and abstract remain otherwise unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds explanations for text supervision providing limited benefit with abundant labels and potentially complicating optimization, explicitly rejecting universal V2T superiority. Calibration discussion acknowledges Supervised as best overall and narrows MVMAE's advantage. Appendix B newly acknowledges missing beta/gamma sensitivity analysis.

D1.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands reproducibility information: 1,200 pretraining epochs, learning rate 0.0002, batch size 64, five warmup epochs, cosine scheduling, sigmoid alignment-weight annealing with steepness 0.02, and gamma fixed at 1. It also documents timing resources and measurements. These are newly disclosed details; the code-access statement is retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds SigLIP 2 and contrasts its objectives with auxiliary text supervision, cites Rusak et al. for InfoNCE, and explicitly acknowledges adapting established paradigms. Most related-work positioning remains unchanged; the Agostini 2024 venue update identifies the same cited work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the seven-section main narrative are retained. Local revisions expand the discussion and method explanation, add an implementation appendix and acknowledgments, move the existing experimental appendix from B to C, and add authorship and publication information.

P2.justification: v4 adds the view-distribution Table 4 and reformats Tables 1–3 to accommodate uncertainty, using smaller type; Table 2 loses a row. All eleven figures retain their contents, with some relocated by text reflow. Journal headers and localized caption/layout edits are also added.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's bare main-table estimates and sparse training specifications, v4 improves assessability through uncertainty reporting and substantial implementation disclosure. Its calibration and V2T discussion better qualifies the evidence. These gains outweigh the reduced Top-5 comparator coverage, although the unexplained BiomedCLIP omission and minimally documented InfoNCE comparison limit the overall improvement.
